summary: The SOP should not be followed as written: rollback before go/no-go 2 is described as lossless, but no backup is taken after writers stop and cross-version PITR is already Unverified, so a restore can drop committed data. Block 3 gates name no evidence, and several Cloud SQL claims are ahead of the quotes in review/docs/sources.json, including a changed S-10 and S-01 wording that does not match the cancel, Terraform, and prepared-transaction claims.

findings.claim: Rollback before go/no-go 2 is described as losing nothing, but the runbook never takes or identifies a backup after writers stop and after CDC drain. The only backup action is "confirm backups" at T-7, and PITR back across the upgrade is already Unverified, so restoring "the pre-upgrade backup" can drop up to a week of committed writes.
findings.evidence: SOP: "T-7 days | Freeze migrations, confirm backups" and "Before go or no-go 2: restore the pre-upgrade backup to a recovery instance on the source version [S-01], then point the apps back. No writes have happened, so nothing is lost." Later: "whether Cloud SQL allows it is Unverified." S-01's recorded quotes include "recovery instance, which is a new instance running the pre-upgrade version" and do not say when that backup is taken or that the restore is lossless. The live S-01 page could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: After writers are stopped and CDC lag is zero, take a backup, record its id and recoverable time, and only then start the upgrade. State that a restore loses every commit after that backup, and drop the claim that nothing is lost.

findings.claim: Go/no-go 2 is called the point of no return while writes are still closed, and the rollback section jumps from "before go/no-go 2" to "after reopening," so the interval between the decision and reopen has no rule. Bringing the pooler up in that same step can also admit writes before anyone reopens them, which makes the "no writes have happened" premise false.
findings.evidence: SOP runbook: "Bring up the pooler and routing, then run validation and smoke tests | App on-call | Go or no-go 2: the point of no return" followed by a separate row "Reopen writes". Rollback only covers "Before go or no-go 2" and "After reopening." "Maintenance mode" is not defined, and nothing says it still blocks writes once the pooler is up.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the lossless window as after the freeze backup and before the first committed write on the new version. Say explicitly that maintenance mode stays on until the reopen step, and give a rollback action for a failed smoke test after go/no-go 2 but before reopen.

findings.claim: Rollback restores a new recovery instance and points apps back, but it never fences the instance that was just upgraded. That instance is still running and can keep accepting writes, so the two copies can diverge.
findings.evidence: SOP: "restore the pre-upgrade backup to a recovery instance on the source version [S-01], then point the apps back." S-01 quote: "recovery instance, which is a new instance running the pre-upgrade version". The live page could not be fetched. The runbook has no step to stop, delete, or otherwise fence the upgraded instance before the cut back.
findings.suggested_fix: In the rollback steps, require the upgraded instance to be fenced or deleted before connection strings move, and record that check next to the recovery-instance id.

findings.claim: Block 3 exit gates have no evidence column. G3.1 can be marked done because "validation passed," and G3.4 because "Close-out is done," without a linked artifact, which is a gate passing on say-so.
findings.evidence: G0–G2 tables have an Evidence column. The Block 3 table does not: "G3.1 | Production runs the target version, writes are open, and validation passed" and "G3.4 | Close-out is done". The short version still says a block exits only when every gate is Done with linked evidence or Waived. G2.4 requires a plan diff for the same 2x check that G3.3 leaves unnamed.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each G3 row the same evidence style as Block 2: version output, validate.sql output, consumer check log, plan diff, and a close-out checklist with backup-retention and clone-deletion links.

findings.claim: The SOP states as fact that a replica-inclusive Cloud SQL upgrade cannot be cancelled and cannot be run from Terraform. The recorded S-01 quotes support only a cancel-window limit and a fragment about the console and Terraform; they do not mention replicas or running the upgrade.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Cloud SQL can cancel only during the main upgrade phase, and not when replicas are included [S-01]." Also: "Google says replica-inclusive upgrades can't run from Terraform [S-01]" and "through gcloud [S-07] or the API, which rules out cancelling [S-01]." S-01 quotes: "You can only cancel during the main upgrade phase" and "you can't use the Google Cloud console or Terraform". Appendix B question 6 treats S-31 against S-01 as a real conflict. The live S-01 page could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the full S-01 cancel sentence, label anything it does not literally say as Unverified, and separate "cannot cancel this way" from "cannot start a replica-inclusive upgrade from Terraform" before keeping question 6.

findings.claim: The SOP says Cloud SQL's precheck reports prepared transactions, which are the two-phase-commit rows that block pg_upgrade. The S-01 quote says prepared statements, which are a different object and do not block pg_upgrade.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Cloud SQL's precheck also reports prepared transactions [S-01]." S-01 quote: "Uncommitted prepared statements". Kit section 6b correctly queries pg_prepared_xacts. The live S-01 page could not be fetched, so the quote could not be read in context.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-read the Cloud SQL sentence and name the object it actually checks. If it is PREPARE TRANSACTION, quote that wording; if it is prepared statements, do not treat it as the pg_upgrade blocker.

findings.claim: S-10 is marked changed, and sources.md says claims that cite a changed source stay Unverified until rechecked. The SOP still states the ALTER EXTENSION behavior as a settled fact.
findings.evidence: review/docs/sources.md: "A source whose quotes have moved is marked changed ... Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks." review/docs/sources.json S-10 status is "changed". SOP: "Cloud SQL maintenance installs new binaries but doesn't update extension versions [S-10]." The same citation is repeated at the Block 2 ALTER EXTENSION step and in the reading guide section 8f.
findings.suggested_fix: Label every S-10 claim Unverified until the quote check is green again, and say the rehearsal must show whether ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE is still required.

findings.claim: The 10 million large-object limit and the 100,000-relation guidance are instance-wide, but the kit counts them per database and neither the SOP nor the reading guide tells anyone to sum every precheck file. A per-database green result can hide an instance that will fail or time out.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Cloud SQL's MVU fails above 10 million large objects in total [S-01]" and "tuned for up to about 100,000 relations". S-01 quotes: "more than 10 million large objects, then the upgrade fails" and "up to around 100,000 relations". precheck.sql sections 2d and 2e count pg_class and pg_largeobject_metadata in the connected database only. Reading guide: "The sum is well under 100,000" for section 2d of one file. G0.3's provider precheck is a backstop only if that precheck reports these limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an instance rollup: sum large objects and relations across every precheck file, compare those totals to the Cloud SQL limits, and make the rollup evidence for G0.4.

findings.claim: The CDC drain query reads every replication slot. Physical slots, which a primary with replicas has, have a null confirmed_flush_lsn, so lag_bytes is null and the instruction to drain "until the lag is zero" cannot be met as written.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Stop writers and drain CDC until the lag is zero" followed by "SELECT slot_name, pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) AS lag_bytes FROM pg_replication_slots". The query does not filter slot_type = 'logical'. A null lag is not zero, and the runbook gives no other success condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the drain check to logical slots, treat a null confirmed_flush_lsn as not drained, and name the leftover slot that must be dropped or ignored before the upgrade starts.

findings.claim: G1.1 says every G0.3 and G0.4 blocker is fixed in production, but the evidence is only a rerun of kit sections 6a–6g. Provider-precheck blockers such as pg_ivm, PostGIS, large-object totals, and database count are not in those sections, so the gate can pass while Cloud SQL would still refuse the upgrade.
findings.evidence: SOP gate: "G1.1 | Every blocker from G0.3 and G0.4 is fixed in production on the source version, and a rerun of the kit shows it clear | Rerun of kit sections 6a to 6g". G0.3 evidence is "Precheck JSON and operations describe JSON". The blocker list also includes pg_ivm, PostGIS 3.6.0, and the 10 million large-object failure, which the reading guide places in provider output and kit sections 2 and 3, not 6a–6g.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a fresh provider precheck JSON with no ERROR rows as G1.1 evidence, plus the kit sections that actually contained each blocker.

findings.claim: G1.4 requires every password-login role to be SCRAM, with evidence "Role rows," but the SOP also says managed-service roles cannot read pg_authid. Section 7 only shows password_encryption, which controls new passwords and does not prove stored hashes are SCRAM, so the gate is either a waiver or a false pass.
findings.evidence: SOP: "G1.4 | Password-login roles use SCRAM, or each MD5 role has its owner's waiver | Role rows" and "On managed services nobody can read pg_authid [S-05], so test every password login on the rehearsal clone." Reading guide: "md5 means new passwords are still MD5". The login test is not G1.4 evidence and happens only in Block 2. S-05 quotes do not mention pg_authid; the live page could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Change G1.4 evidence to an owner-signed login test on the clone for every password role, and state that SHOW password_encryption does not prove existing hashes. Allow a named waiver only when that test cannot be run.

findings.claim: G0.5 reconciles logical slots, publications, and pglogical nodes, but not subscriptions. The kit lists subscriptions, and a database that is a subscriber can break or silently stop applying changes after a major upgrade without an owner or a plan.
findings.evidence: SOP G0.5: "Every logical slot, publication and pglogical node maps to a named consumer". precheck.sql section 4b also runs "SELECT subname, subenabled FROM pg_subscription". Reading guide: "Subscriptions mean this instance also consumes from somewhere." No task or gate assigns those rows an owner or a target-version plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add subscriptions to G0.5 with an owner, remote publisher, and a recreate-or-refresh step in the runbook, including how the subscriber's position is checked after cutover.

findings.claim: The logical branch replaces Block 2 steps 4 through 12, which removes the rehearsed CDC steady state, validation, stats and analyze work, and pooler and replica routing. It does not say which G2 gates still apply, so a connection-string cutover can be approved without those checks.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Use this only if the decision record picks a logical migration. It replaces Block 2 steps 4 to 12." Steps 4–12 include the test CDC consumer, the upgrade and ANALYZE, slot recreate, "Run the validation scripts and smoke tests", and "Bring the pooler and replica routing up". Gates G2.3–G2.7 still require stats, plan diffs, CDC checks, and a routing log. The logical section ends at "Cutover becomes a connection-string switch."
findings.suggested_fix: State which G2 gates remain for a logical migration and replace only the upgrade command. Keep validation, CDC proof, routing, and the two timed rehearsals as exit criteria.

findings.claim: The cutover abort rule "rehearsed time plus 25%" does not match the 75% window gate, so the wait-or-restore decision can fire too early or after the window is already gone. The same line says to restore without saying that a restore starts only after cancel succeeds or the operation has finished.
findings.evidence: G2.1: "Two rehearsals in a row finish the in-window steps within 75% of the window". Block 3 checkpoint: "Past the rehearsed time plus 25%, decide whether to wait or restore. Cloud SQL can cancel only during the main upgrade phase". S-01 quote: "You can only cancel during the main upgrade phase". 125% of a rehearsal that used the full 75% is 93.75% of the window; 125% of a much shorter rehearsal abandons a window that still fits. "In-window steps" is not defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the abort clock as a fraction of the approved window, list which steps count, and write that a restore starts only after the upgrade operation is cancelled or has ended in failure.

findings.claim: G2.1 can pass on timing sheets from a clone that is a smaller tier, has no replicas, or has a cold cache. The SOP names that mismatch as a risk and never makes matching shape evidence for the gate, so the production window can still be missed.
findings.evidence: G2.1 evidence is "Two timing sheets" only. Risks: "A rehearsal that doesn't match production: a different tier, no replicas, or a cold cache." Step 1 notes "Cloud SQL clones don't copy replicas [S-06]" and step 2 adds replicas only "if the plan upgrades them". No gate compares tier, disk, or replica count to production.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a G2 evidence row that the clone's tier, disk, and replica topology match production, or a signed waiver that states how the timings were scaled.

findings.claim: The kit is written for PostgreSQL 14 to 18, but G0.6's decision record does not require the source version's support deadline. The source pack already records that community 14 updates stop in November 2026 and Cloud SQL extended support for 14 starts on 2027-02-01, and a target date can be signed without them.
findings.evidence: precheck.sql: "Written for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 14 -> 18." G0.6 covers "path, target, window, data-loss rule, rollback approach, go or no-go owner and target date" and does not mention support end. S-21 quote: "will stop releasing updates for the 14.X release series in November 2026". S-02 quotes include "February 1, 2027" and "February 1, 2030". B0-10 says only "Version research for this source and target pair, with sources." The SOP never cites S-02 or S-21.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a G0.6 field for the source version's community and provider support dates, cited from S-21 and S-02, and block the target date when it falls in extended support unless the business approver waives the cost.

findings.claim: The stats gate compares pg_stats counts and treats a stable count as proof that every table has planner stats. pg_stats only shows tables the caller can see, so a database owner who does not own every table can satisfy G2.3 while other tables have no stats. The SOP warns that ANALYZE skips those tables and does not apply the same limit to the count.
findings.evidence: SOP baseline: "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stats WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')" and "If the stats count held: don't run plain --analyze-in-stages". G2.3: "After the upgrade every table has planner stats, or the analyze step covers the gap". S-16 quote: "will skip over any tables that the calling user does not have permission to analyze". The missing-stats query in step 9 uses the same pg_stats view.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the count and the missing-stats query as a role that owns every user table, or union one result per owner, and make G2.3 evidence that list rather than a single count.

findings.claim: Guardrails are described as enforced by the plugin's rules and hook. The reviewed plugin tree has the precheck kit and its reading guide only, so a team cannot find a control that blocks production access.
findings.evidence: SOP: "These are enforced by the plugin's rules and hook" linking to ../plugins/pg-major-upgrade/. The files under review/plugins/pg-major-upgrade/ are assets/precheck.sql and skills/pg-upgrade-precheck/references/precheck-reading-guide.md. Section 7 also states the rules in prose: no production credentials, PRs only, people run production commands.
findings.suggested_fix: Point the sentence at the actual rules and hook files, or state that the guardrail is policy until those controls are present.

findings.claim: The SOP states that on managed services nobody can read pg_authid and cites Cloud SQL's users page. That row's quotes do not mention pg_authid, and the adapting section says provider facts should be marked Cloud SQL.
findings.evidence: SOP: "On managed services nobody can read pg_authid [S-05], so test every password login on the rehearsal clone." S-05 quotes: "customers cannot create or have access to users with superuser attributes" and "Creating replication publications and subscriptions". The supports blurb mentions pg_statistic, not pg_authid. The live page could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the sentence Cloud SQL, cite a quote that actually names pg_authid or cloudsqlsuperuser, and tell other providers to test whether their admin role can read it.

findings.claim: The reading guide says any large object blocks a logical path. The SOP says large objects are not replicated, and the S-13 quote list does not say the migration fails or that every large object must be removed.
findings.evidence: Reading guide section 2e red flag: "Any large objects at all block logical paths [S-13]." SOP logical branch: "Unlogged tables and large objects don't replicate". S-13 quotes: "Large Object data type" and "UNLOGGED and TEMPORARY tables aren't and can't be replicated". The live page could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Say large objects are omitted from the logical copy and must be migrated or waived by their owner. Reserve "block" for conditions that abort the upgrade.

findings.claim: Slot survival from PostgreSQL 17 is labeled Inferred from S-14 and S-22, but neither row's quotes mention replication slots. A provider other than Cloud SQL can follow that inference and skip recreating slots that the upgrade actually drops.
findings.evidence: SOP: "slots only survive pg_upgrade from a source of 17 or later (Inferred from S-14 and S-22)." S-14 quotes are "will transfer most optimizer statistics", "custom statistics added by an extension, or statistics collected by the cumulative statistics system", and "--swap". S-22 quotes cover NOT NULL constraints, aclitem, prepared transactions, regcollation, and output_plugin_libraries. The live pages could not be fetched. Cloud SQL is separately cited as deleting every logical slot [S-01].
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the pg_upgrade sentence that actually describes slot migration, or mark slot survival Unverified and keep "create new slots and record the old LSN" for every provider until a rehearsal shows the slots still exist.

findings.claim: Appendix A lists incompatibilities that do not fail pg_upgrade and are not in any Block 1 task or gate: full-text and pg_trgm reindex on non-libc clusters, primary/foreign key collation rules, and the PostgreSQL 16 CREATEROLE change. A team that executes the gates can miss wrong search results or broken role scripts.
findings.evidence: Appendix A: "Full-text search and pg_trgm indexes need a reindex on non-libc clusters | DBA, if ICU or builtin | S-17" and "PK and FK pairs must use deterministic or matching nondeterministic collations | S-17". S-17 quotes: "recommended to reindex all indexes related to full-text search and pg_trgm" and "Require primary/foreign key relationships to use either deterministic collations". CREATEROLE is under S-19. B1-01 through B1-12 do not mention collation provider, those reindexes, or CREATEROLE.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Block 1 check for the collation provider and nondeterministic keys, put any required reindex in the timed runbook, and add CREATEROLE to the role-script review.

findings.claim: The rehearsal cites Flink CDC startup modes that can skip a snapshot and does not mention the project's own source that postgres-cdc documents only PostgreSQL 9.6 through 14. A team can plan a no-snapshot resume on a connector that the source list does not support for 18.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Flink CDC has latest-offset and committed-offset startup modes [S-27]. Whether a consumer can skip the snapshot is Inferred, so this step tests it." S-26 quote: "9.6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 | JDBC Driver: 42.5.1" with supports text "Flink CDC's postgres-cdc lists PostgreSQL 9.6 to 14." G1.3 requires a connector version that supports the target but does not cite S-26.
findings.suggested_fix: In the CDC step, cite S-26 next to S-27 and require the connector's documented major-version range before choosing a startup mode that skips the snapshot.

findings.claim: The Block 0 task gives the gcloud precheck command without --target-database-version, which is the only flag recorded for S-08. The full command exists only in precheck.sql comments, so a DBA following the task table can run a different command than the kit describes.
findings.evidence: SOP B0-04: "gcloud sql instances pre-check-major-version-upgrade [S-07, S-08]". S-08 quote: "target-database-version". precheck.sql comments: "gcloud sql instances pre-check-major-version-upgrade INSTANCE --target-database-version=POSTGRES_18 --project=PROJECT --format=json". The live reference page could not be fetched to confirm the flag is mandatory.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the full precheck command, including target version, project, and json output, in B0-04 so the task and the kit match.

findings.claim: The SOP says all four catalog blocker classes are Verified in pg_upgrade's checks [S-22]. The recorded quotes cover aclitem, regcollation, prepared transactions, and inconsistent NOT NULL constraints, and do not include system composite types or databases pg_upgrade cannot connect to.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Any row in kit section 6a (reg* types, aclitem, system composite types), 6b (prepared transactions), 6c (databases pg_upgrade can't connect to) or 6d (child columns missing a parent NOT NULL) blocks pg_upgrade 18. All four are Verified in pg_upgrade's own checks [S-22]." S-22 quotes: "Your installation contains inconsistent NOT NULL constraints", "Checking for incompatible \"aclitem\" data type", "The source cluster contains prepared transactions", "regcollation", "output_plugin_libraries". The supports text names datallowconn, but that string is not a quote. check.c could not be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the check.c strings for system composites and datallowconn to S-22, or label 6a system composites and 6c Unverified until those quotes are on the row.
